source.section: PDF page 19, Table A (Single column, 'More Than 30,000 / Less Than or Equal To 31,000: 14,000'); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 31,000.00 = 31,000.00. Federal taxable income = 31,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 15,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 31,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 31,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 31,000.00 - 0.00 = 31,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 31,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 31,000.00 is more than 30,000.00, exemption 14,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 31,000.00 - 14,000.00 = 17,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 17,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 7,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 315.00 = 515.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 31,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 515.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.15 (Connecticut AGI 31,000.00 is in the band more than 26,500.00); Line 9 = 515.00 x 0.15 = 77.25. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 515.00 - 77.25 = 437.75 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI exactly 31,000 is in the band 'more than 30,000, less than or equal to 31,000', so the exemption is 14,000, not 13,000.
